questions.stem: Which Biochemical method is exploited for monoclonal antibody production by hybridoma technique?
questions.solutionHtml:
Purine Salvage pathway
  • Purine salvage pathway is utilized by monoclonal antibodies in hybridoma technology.
  • In hybridoma technique monoclonal antibodies are produced using the HAT medium which contains hypoxanthine, thymidylate & aminopterin.
  • Hybrid cells are cultured in HAT medium and monoclonal antibodies are obtained as substrate for the salvage pathway for purine nucleotides production.


Satyanarayan Biochemistry, 4th Edition, Page No. 730,731.

questions.stem: In which of the following organisms’ genetic material is adenine not equal to thymine?
questions.solutionHtml:
HIV
  • HIV virus belongs to the retrovirus family having ssRNA genome. Hence the no. Of adenine need not be equal to the thymine residues in the single strand.
  • Single-stranded DNA, and RNAs which are usually single-stranded, do not obey Chargaff’s rule. However, double-stranded RNA which is the genetic material in certain viruses satisfies Chargaff’s rule.


Satyanarayan Biochemistry, 4th Edition, Page No.74

questions.stem: Phase 1 reaction of xenobiotics, called hydroxylation involving cytochrome p450. In this reaction cyt p450 need which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
NADPH
  • The cyt. p450 enzymes use electrons provided by NADPH for the hydroxylation reaction.
  • The main reaction involved in phase 1 metabolism is hydroxylation, catalyzed by a family of enzymes known as monooxygenases or cytochromes P450.
  • At least half of the common drugs that we ingest are metabolized by isoforms of cytochrome P450. They also act on steroid hormones, carcinogens, and pollutants.
  • The overall reaction catalyzed by cytochrome P450 is: RH + O2 + NADPH + H+ → R-OH + H2O + NADP


Harper’s Illustrated Biochemistry, 31st Edition, Page No.116

questions.stem: Which of the following about the electron transport chain are CORRECT?It is located in the inner mitochondrion membraneCytochrome C accepts electrons from complex IIComplex I is called NADH dehydrogenaseCoenzyme Q accepts electrons from complex I and complex II Choose the correct answer from the given code:

options.label: B
options.text: If a and d are correct

options.label: C
options.text: If a, c and, d are correct

options.label: D
options.text: If all four (a, b, c, & d) are correct

questions.answerText: If a, c and, d are correct
questions.solutionHtml:
If a, c and, d are correct

It is located in the inner mitochondrion membrane

  • The major components of ETC are located in IMM. 
  • There are four fixed protein complexes (Complex I-IV) embedded in the membrane. 
  • There are two soluble electron carriers CoQ and Cyt c
  • The CoQ moves freely in the membrane
  • Cyt c is present in the intermembrane space

Complex I is called NADH dehydrogenase

  • Complex I has FMN and Fe-S centers with NADH dehydrogenase enzyme activity. 
  • It takes electrons from NADH (get oxidized) and transfers them to ubiquinone (gets reduced), hence is called NADH-Q oxidoreductase. 

Coenzyme Q accepts electrons from complex I and complex II

  • Ubiquinone or Q is a movable electron carrier and accepts electrons from both complex I (NADH) and complex II (FADH2)
  • It can accept either one or two electrons at a time.

Cytochrome C accepts electrons from complex II

  • Cytochrome c accepts electrons from complex III and not from complex II
  • It transfers electrons to complex IV.


Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 124

questions.stem: Which of the following is complementary to the active site of the enzyme?
questions.solutionHtml:
Substrate
  • The substrate is always complementary to the active site of enzyme with which it is supposed to bind.


Satyanarayan Biochemistry, 4th Edition, Page No. 98,99

questions.stem: Which of the following is not involved in the repair of DNA following double- stranded breaks?
questions.solutionHtml:
MSH2
  • MSH 2 gene codes for DNA mismatch repair protein.
  • Rest of the given genes codes for proteins involved in repair of double-stranded DNA breaks.


Henrys clinical diagnosis and management by laboratory methods, 23rd edition, page no - 1305-1310

questions.stem: A 60- year old lady with diabetes mellitus comes with dizziness. Which of the following would be seen in a patient with hyperinsulinemia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Increased fatty acid synthesis
  • Insulin is an anabolic hormone that promotes the storage of nutrients.
  • In conditions of hyperinsulinemia (elevated levels of insulin), there is an increased tendency for the synthesis of fatty acids and storage of triglycerides.
  • This is because insulin enhances the uptake of glucose and promotes its conversion into fatty acids through lipogenesis.


Harrison’s Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page No.3086
